title: Moving-platform following and landing
description: Onboard vision enables an aerial robot to detect, follow and land on a moving ground platform.
introduction: A ground robot can extend the possibilities of an aerial mission, but the UAV must first reach it safely. This work connects visual relative-pose estimation with autonomous following and landing on a moving platform.

problem.heading: Return to a platform that keeps moving.
paragraphs: A mobile ground platform offers a potential support point for aerial operations. Following and landing must account for its motion.
Relative pose must therefore connect visual perception to trajectory planning and flight control.

approach.heading: Use visual markers to guide the approach.
paragraphs: An onboard monocular camera observes ArUco fiducial markers on the ground platform. The estimated relative pose feeds a trajectory planner and decoupled controllers.
These generate velocity set-points for the UAV autopilot's inner control loops. Perception, planning and set-point generation run onboard the aerial robot.

evidence.label: Digital-twin evaluation
evidence.text: The system was tested in a solar-farm digital twin using ROS, Gazebo and ArduPilot software-in-the-loop.

evidence.label: Outdoor following and landing
evidence.text: Physical experiments at Instituto Superior Técnico used a hexacopter and a modified Jackal ground robot.
